# Transportation Impact Brief — Dana (PERSONA-009)
**South Portland FY27 Budget | Transportation Segment Guide**

---

## Executive Summary

The South Portland school board is moving toward a vote on a configuration that the administration confirmed, at the March 30, 2026 meeting, has not been modeled for transportation impact — and will not be before the vote. The administration's own survey data shows 90% of parents worried about busing complications. Independent analysis puts the fiscal exposure for the recommended Option A at **$946,449–$1,679,845 annually**, or up to 112% of the savings the administration is claiming. That is your lede.

---

## Key Finding

**Under Option A, the district's claimed savings could be entirely erased — and then some.**

The administration has not quantified the transportation cost of its recommended configuration. Outside analysis shows total annual fiscal exposure at **43%–112% of claimed savings** under Option A. At the high end, the district and affected families together absorb more in new costs than the budget cut is projected to save.

This figure is not in any district document. It was not presented to the board.

---

## Configuration Comparison

| Metric | Option A *(recommended)* | Option B | Variant C |
|---|---|---|---|
| Families split across buildings | 139–169 | **0** | 123–150 |
| Bus drivers needed | 30 | 24 | 29 |
| Drivers currently available (post-cut) | 17–20 | 17–20 | 17–20 |
| **Driver shortfall** | **−10 to −13** | **−4 to −7** | **−9 to −12** |
| Bus tiers required | 3–4 | 3 | 3–4 |
| Families facing new care gap | 42–144 | **0** | 37–128 |
| Annual family care cost burden | $143,640–$803,520 | **$0** | $126,540–$714,240 |
| District annual cost | $802,809–$876,325 | $30,365–$79,908 | $670,073–$735,597 |
| **Total annual fiscal exposure** | **$946,449–$1,679,845** | **$30,365–$79,908** | **$796,613–$1,449,837** |
| Exposure as % of claimed savings | 43%–112% | 1.4%–5.3% | 36%–97% |

**Driver shortfall is universal.** Even Option B — the lowest-impact choice — is short 4–7 drivers. The 14% SEA staffing cut that created this gap was decided before anyone counted the drivers or modeled the routes (confirmed: Director of Operations Mike Natalie, March 30, 2026 meeting).

---

## What's Missing

The district has not produced any of the following before the scheduled vote:

- **A route model.** Transportation logistics are described as "underway with a partner" but will be operationalized after the board votes, not before. No route counts, no timing projections, no cost estimates are in the public record.
- **A driver math reconciliation.** The administration has not publicly acknowledged the shortfall between the 20 confirmed drivers (post-cut: 17–20) and the 24–30 required under any configuration.
- **A 4th-tier cost estimate.** Options A and C may require a 4th bus tier for grade-band routing. The driver idle window (9:30 AM–1:30 PM) leaves no margin for a 4th tier without overtime. No overtime cost projection exists.
- **A before/after care capacity analysis.** After-care is full at 4 of 5 schools. The only school with openings is Kaler — which closes under Option A. The district has not modeled where 42–144 newly displaced families would go.
- **A McKinney-Vento cost projection.** Annual MV exposure ranges from $54,337–$127,853 under Option A. No district document acknowledges this liability.
- **An explanation for the 50.2% transport cost spike.** South Portland's per-pupil transport costs rose from $709 (FY23) to $1,065 (FY25) — 50.2% — against a statewide average increase of 10.5%. No cause has been formally documented.

---

## Limitations

This analysis is built on public budget documents, board meeting recordings, and independent modeling. It is not a district-produced document. Range estimates reflect genuine uncertainty in family counts and cost assumptions — the district holds the data that would narrow these ranges. The route expansion cost figure ($748,472 for Option A) is the weakest single input in the model; it is derived from per-route cost extrapolation, not a contracted quote.

This analysis cannot tell you which configuration the board will choose, what the consultant will recommend, or whether the vote will be delayed.

---

## Invitation to Improve

The district can sharpen every range in this brief with four data points it already holds:

1. **Current route map and driver assignments** — narrows the shortfall estimate
2. **Before/after care enrollment figures by school** — narrows the care gap range
3. **The transportation consultant's scope of work and timeline** — establishes whether route modeling will precede or follow the vote
4. **The FY25 transport cost breakdown** — resolves the 50.2% anomaly

This brief will be updated to reflect any data the district provides before the vote.
